reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is TP: User input from request.getParameter() flows through param -> bar (via .replace("\"", """) ) -> response.getWriter().println(). While double quotes are escaped, the sink uses single-quoted HTML attributes ('data-name'). Attackers can bypass double-quote escaping by injecting single-quote-based payloads (e.g., ' onclick=alert(1)) that break out of the attribute boundary. Resolved sink value depends on user parameter, not a constant.

evidence.note: User input flows to response via incomplete sanitization - only double quotes escaped, single quotes remain unescaped enabling XSS
